environment.database: fresh local disposable PostgreSQL 16 service on the GitHub Actions runner

corrections: Provider total timing now starts before the sync service is invoked rather than after its promise is created.
The first-commit observer handles both sync fulfillment and rejection without producing a detached rejected promise.
The first-commit observer performs a final database observation after sync settlement.
Unexpected network requests are blocked outside the explicit synthetic provider stubs.
Worker-wave output records benchmark poll and observer intervals and that the job was queued before worker startup.
The disposable database name requires a ci, test, or benchmark token rather than an arbitrary substring.
limitations: Provider responses were synthetic and removed network latency, rate limits, retries, and archive/window variability.
PostgreSQL was local to the CI runner rather than Neon.
The engine was WASM rather than the documented local-binary Render worker.
First-import timing was observed with a 2 ms database poll, adding observer latency and local database load.
Worker-wave timing began after the job was queued and immediately started an in-process worker; idle polling, deployment wake, and external queue delay were excluded.
Three-sample depth-12 and worker-wave p90 values equal the observed maximum and are not stable production percentiles.
The preparation parent and reconciler are not implemented, so complete onboarding duration was not measured.
